name: Ash Register
summary: The Ash Vault's full ritual of the broken ceiling: an unbroken shell, the whole recovery recorded publicly, and the fragments never displayed again. It exists because a great ascension is a fire-affinity body opened on a purpose, so the culture has no temples and no museum - it has a register, and the register is the only relic it keeps.

attributes.language: A liturgical register in which the past is always in the third person and the failure is always present tense, because the recovery is still happening and has not concluded.
attributes.values: Nothing broken is displayed; a record is complete or it is not kept; the dead are counted publicly rather than mourned privately.
attributes.etiquette: Grief is expressed by reading the register aloud in full. Questions about the failure are answered factually and at length; pity is refused, and its refusal is delivered without heat.
attributes.clothing: Plain, undyed, and closed at the throat, on the argument that an open collar in a chamber holding fragments is an invitation rather than a comfort.
attributes.cuisine: One dish, prepared from what the last recovery left, served to everyone at once at the same table, with no hierarchy of portions - the abolition of ranked plates was the culture's founding act.
attributes.art: No visual art of any kind. The register itself is the art form: a wall of plain entries, and the culture's entire aesthetic argument is that this is more moving than a painting.
attributes.architecture: Buildings with no display case, no alcove and no interior shrine, built around a single walled court where the register is read aloud and nothing else is kept.
attributes.festivals: The Whole Reading - held when a chamber is opened after a sealing, when the entire recovered record is read in one sitting and everyone present must remain for all of it.
attributes.marriage: A contract of mutual witnessing, agreed in advance and honoured by attendance rather than sentiment, on the reasoning that two people who will not sit through eight hours of a reading have not agreed to much.
attributes.taboos: No fragment carried out of the chamber; no fragment offered as a gift; no private collection of anything from the fire; and no account of the broken ceiling given by anyone who was not there.
attributes.cause: History: the attempt to cross the immortal border as a permanent passage ended in the Eighteenth Bed Collapse, and this is the culture of the chamber the failure was sealed in rather than a theory about why it failed.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The chamber's wardens and its readers are Commonborn and Emberblood in roughly equal number and the office does not care which; the culture is an institution's grief, and the fire is what it happened to.
attributes.death_rites: A name is added to the register and read by someone other than the household; a death is not a private matter here, it is an entry, and it is entered the same day.

name: Blind Survey
summary: A culture that maps by echo and counts by listening, and whose entire professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until someone has heard it. It exists because the mortal tier seats no spatial law, so the world cannot reliably report its own size or change its dimensions - and the one instrument that returns a consistent answer in a frame whose geometry drifts is sound.

attributes.language: A spoken language whose long vowels carry range and whose short vowels carry distance, so ordinary conversation is a continuous survey and speakers are casually incapable of discussing a room's proportions.
attributes.values: Every figure is a range until it has been heard twice; a surveyor who has not slept declares it; the inaccessible is not absent and is reported as inaccessible.
attributes.etiquette: Unwanted noise is an interruption of work and is apologised for with genuine embarrassment; asking someone to describe a thing while watching them is treated as asking them to do it badly on purpose.
attributes.clothing: Soft, close and quiet, with hard soles for working surfaces; this is the only guild in the setting where the loudest garment is the uniform and being loud in it is a badge.
attributes.cuisine: Food chosen and prepared for sound as much as for taste, with quiet courses and a deliberate practice of eating in company in silence - the meal is the one place the guild is not surveying anything.
attributes.art: Architecture played as an instrument. The guild's buildings are tuned: corridors, stairwells and culverts are designed to be struck and listened to, and a hall that returns a dead note is considered a defective hall.
attributes.architecture: Survey halls, tuned chambers and deliberately unequal stairwells: every floor is planned so that a door can be closed and a note taken, and the buildings are therefore shaped by an acoustic plan rather than a circulation one.
attributes.festivals: The Full Silence, one night in which nobody in the guild makes any sound at all, and which the surrounding villages treat as an emergency until they learn what it is.
attributes.marriage: A pairing agreed by the two households on the strength of a shared sounding, which the guild treats as more binding than a vow and which outsiders find the strangest single sentence in the setting.
attributes.taboos: No figure published with its range omitted; no surveying during a survey; no speaking inside a sounding gallery; and no declaring a place empty, only unmeasured.
attributes.cause: Cosmology: spatial_law is unwritten in a three-slot frame, so the world has no fixed geometry and no process runs on it - and a people who cannot trust the frame chose the one sense that travels inside it.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: The perception-built body cannot take the Body path and reads a strained qi more finely than anything else here, which makes sound a better instrument for it - but the culture was taught to children of every body and refuses to be described as an affinity.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Its teachers include Commonborn and Stoneborn whom it trained from nothing, and the culture's own doctrine is that hearing is a skill; the affinity raised the invitation, the guild did the teaching.
attributes.death_rites: The room of the dead is sounded once, fully, by three people who are never told what they heard, and the three reports are compared only for whether they agree - and a disagreement ends the conversation without a verdict.

name: Breakwater
summary: A stone-shored coastal culture that reads water, sand and wind for a living, because after the Iron Grief that reading was the only work on the plains that still bought passage. It exists because the mortal tier's only caging ore ran out at the seam, and a population with no way to climb could only sell what it could see.

attributes.language: A work register heavy with position and none with tense; a statement of what a thing is doing matters and a statement of when it did it does not, because the current has already revised the when.
attributes.values: Nothing that cannot be carried is built; a wall that cannot be repaired by the people it shelters is decoration; a warning given late is worse than none given.
attributes.etiquette: A question about the sea is asked plainly and answered exactly. A question about the sea asked as conversation is read as a mistake in the asker and is not corrected.
attributes.clothing: Layered oilskin over heavy plate, fastened inside, because on this coast the wind gets under a coat before the water does and every fastening must survive being used one-handed in a swell.
attributes.art: Slope and gradient cut as public marks into stone that faces the water - a gallery of the sea's known moods, kept by addition, never redone, so the wall is also the only unaltered record anyone kept.
attributes.cuisine: Salt, and nothing that has travelled. The shore diet is what the last boat put in, which is why every cook here is an excellent improviser and a poor planner, and why the wall crews eat before a tide and not after.
attributes.architecture: Dry-stone mass on the exposed face, mortared brick to leeward, and a lower storey built to be flooded and reoccupied rather than defended, which the culture regards as the whole point of a harbour.
attributes.festivals: The Standing Water, when the first wave of the season runs past a marked point that was previously safe, and the harbour is read from the whole shoreline at once.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract witnessed by whoever was on the wall at the time, which means most pairings here are witnessed by strangers and the culture has decided that is sufficient.
attributes.taboos: No masonry laid in haste above the high-water mark; no refusal to answer a water question; no building of anything that cannot be moved by two people who are not strong.
attributes.cause: History and ecology together: the Iron Grief ended the ascent and left a population with bodies and no ladder, on shores where the only currency left was knowing where not to build.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: One race holds the craft and four are welcome in it, and the culture's own accounting admits the Tower was never its bloodline but its customer.
attributes.death_rites: A stone from the grave is cut back into the wall, so a settled coast eventually buries its own dead in its own defences and considers this a continuation rather than a desecration.

name: Charterhouse
summary: The roadside house that sells the one commodity the crossings charge for: a bed, a hot meal and a person the Marshal's clerks will accept as a guarantor. It exists because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a body and the law forbids levying a seat, so travel had to be underwritten by somebody with no stake in the border.

attributes.language: A trade pidgin assembled from every body's speech, with a single written form for numbers of people and no written form for anything else.
attributes.values: A guest who can pay for another is a guest who will be back; information about a route is worth more than a night's bed; no house admits anyone to whom a debt is owed.
attributes.etiquette: Prices are stated once at the door and never adjusted at the table. A traveller who argues at the door is offered the yard, which is free and has no bed. Asking a guest where they are from is how you learn their trade, never their origin.
attributes.clothing: The house provides a dyed half-cloak on arrival, dusty on departure, and a house holds the right to read colour as a station in the road - which is why every traveller outside a city wears the wrong one.
attributes.cuisine: One stew kept at simmer from the first light and never allowed to finish, thickened with whatever grain the last house paid in. It is thin, it is identical in every house on a road, and this sameness is the house's real product.
attributes.art: Blazed milestone notation on every doorpost - not decoration but a running tally of arrivals, departures and disturbances, read by the next house as if the road had a ledger.
attributes.architecture: One room, one barred door, one ledger desk within reach of the fire, and a stable whose floor is cut with hoof-lines that a host counts nightly against the ration.
attributes.festivals: The Safe Conduct - a night with no room charged and every debt paused, held once, on whatever night the road has been quiet longest, so the date is named after the event.
attributes.marriage: A guest who stays past two seasons and takes a household name has married in by use; there is no rite, only the house quietly moving the second bowl to the family shelf.
attributes.taboos: No house may hold a sealed item for a guest, no guest's name is read from the book aloud, and no house tells another house what it is owed.
attributes.cause: History and arithmetic: the crossing's unit is a person, so the scarcity was never goods but consent - and consent has to be bought by somebody who is not the Marshal.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: A Stoneborn porter and a Tidecaller pedlar share this culture because the culture buys discretion, and discretion is priced by conduct rather than by body.
attributes.death_rites: The dead are given to the ground under a stone that names the house and the road, not the lineage, because no house on a road may keep its dead - there is nowhere to put them that cannot be inherited.

name: Cinder Mark
summary: Not a people but a scar that behaves like one: the households the Cinder Famine left, still holding themselves to the eating rules of the year there was nothing to eat. It exists because a famine imposes its manners fastest on those too young to remember the reason, and a rule learned in infancy outlives the belief that prompted it.

attributes.language: A shared inventory lexicon with no grammar of leisure - the vocabulary of stores is the only vocabulary these households taught their children deliberately, and it shows.
attributes.values: Nothing is wasted and nothing is hoarded; the last portion on the plate is the largest obligation a person has.
attributes.etiquette: Refusing food is impossible and refusing seconds is an insult; a person who says they are full is understood to have said something else and is fed again privately later.
attributes.clothing: Repaired to exhaustion and then handed down without alteration, because a garment altered is a garment whose value was miscounted.
attributes.art: Conspicuously none, and the absence is deliberate and defended: this culture holds that ornament in a poor house is theft from a hungrier one, and argues the position out loud when visitors find it strange.
attributes.cuisine: Raw, cold or cured, and nothing that needs a fire beyond the store's own lamp - a dish that must be cooked is a dish that must be counted against a fuel nobody in the room has, and this culture will not put a meal and a fire into the same argument.
attributes.architecture: A single store per household with three locks and three keys, so no two can ever both be out; the culture considers two locks a suggestion and three a fact.
attributes.festivals: A counted distribution, held on no date, whenever the season turns and the tally can be made honestly; anything resembling a celebration is considered a lie told to the store.
attributes.marriage: Practical and contracted between two households - the ceremony is a mutual inspection of stores, conducted aloud, which the culture considers more binding than any vow.
attributes.taboos: No second helpings at table in company; no storing of food outside the store; no singing after the distribution; and any hospitality served from a private stock rather than the shared one.
attributes.cause: History: the Cinder Famine, which thinned a population whose fuel was its own body and left behind the customs of the thinning rather than the arithmetic that caused it.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Its most careful keepers are Tidecaller, whose cold-affinity bodies feel the shortage least and are hardest to convince; this is a scar of shortage and a household of habit, not a biology.
attributes.death_rites: Burial is refused by most and permitted by all; where it happens, the grave is unmarked and revisited only when the ground is worked, which is not sentiment but a second use.

name: Deadroad
summary: A cultivator people who measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when they were born, and who treat the whole ladder as arriving late by definition. It exists because the entire remaining mortal ladder was shut from the inside by a frame that seats three laws and admits no humanoid - so a mortal who advanced at all is an exception, and a large enough population of exceptions stops reading itself as exceptional.

attributes.language: A technical trade register in which every noun for a stage also names the law value it saturates at, so conversation about a person is conducted entirely in terms of the frame they were trained under.
attributes.values: The technique is the small part and the frame is everything; a gate was never a wall to be climbed, it was a price the tier set before anyone arrived.
attributes.etiquette: Asking someone's realm is considered crude and asking what their frame seats is considered intimate; the second question is asked only once and never in a group.
attributes.clothing: In the court and in the Frost, by deliberate choice as an argument: these people refuse the settled robe in order to say that no settled frame was ever theirs.
attributes.cuisine: Whatever the frame's local failure produces, which makes this one of the few cultures in the setting whose food is explicitly a diagnostic - salt-free on the plains, roast-heavy in the Frost.
attributes.art: Diagrams. This culture's art is a wall-sized chart of how much of the frame's ceiling was already spent at each person's birth, drawn in the settlement hall and updated only by adding.
attributes.architecture: Settlement halls built with an unroofed roof section over the chart, and thresholds deliberately high so that a cultivator's reinforced frame must be consciously lowered rather than merely ducked.
attributes.festivals: The Pre-Existing Ceiling - a day when the whole hall reads its chart for the dead of the previous year, and every realm named is named with the gate it never reached because the gate was not available.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract carrying an explicit clause on who funds which ascent, because in this culture a marriage is two households merging a ledger they expect to be spent.
attributes.taboos: No claim that a gate was a failure of will; no naming an upper-tier practitioner as an authority on anything; and no frame discussed as though its composition were a matter of opinion rather than arithmetic.
attributes.cause: History and cosmology together: the hundred realms' final mortal gates were shut by the frame rather than fought for, the realm nine verdict that established a ceiling as a limit nobody was issued - and this is the only body of practice in the setting that took that verdict at face value.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: A race ceiling and a tier ceiling are two different numbers and this culture exists precisely because they are: it counts the *lower* of the two as the real one and treats the race's own limit as the part of the story that can be argued with.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: It is a political reading of a cosmology, held by three races and by bodies of none of them; two of its three ranks came from the Second Rank settlement and hold it because of where they were born.
attributes.death_rites: The burnt list - at a settlement funeral the names of every deceased read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the two readings are permitted to differ.

name: Deadwatch
summary: A fifty-year body whose fuel is its own furnace and whose population thinned at exactly the rate it could not stop: the Deadwatch keeps no growing store of the long-lived, and instead holds the year's dead together as a declared group. It exists because the Cinder Famine made every individual short of fuel and made the shortfall collective at once.

attributes.language: A register that shortens as grief does: an official long form for a death in office, a clipped one for everything else, and a shared three-note signal used at a distance where speech is not available.
attributes.values: A short life spent hot is not a lesser life; the dead have standing and the living have work; nobody is to be outlived by someone they trained.
attributes.etiquette: You do not say a survivor's age. You say how much they burned, which is the only measure a furnace body can be praised by without grief becoming its subject.
attributes.clothing: Loose layers of undyed ash-cloth, chosen to be ruined rather than mourned; a furnace body in a fitted coat is an unfit body at work, and the refusal to wear one is the culture's mildest snobbery.
attributes.cuisine: Raw or barely heated, because cooking costs fuel a burning body is already spending on itself; the one hot dish is served at the year's watch and nowhere else.
attributes.art: Sound rather than image: an iron sheet, a hand, and the length of the note is how much of a life was actually spent. A short watch is not a lesser work of art.
attributes.architecture: Unbaked mass, one narrow hall, openings placed for draught because moving hot air is free cooling and a sealed room is a kiln; buildings here are the only ones in the setting designed to be fired and abandoned.
attributes.festivals: The Watch - a night of held breath, the dead kept at the centre of a cold hall, and one register read in which every name of the year is spoken once and no grave is visited.
attributes.marriage: Contractual and provisional, with a declared term, and the culture's one indecision: it will not decide for anyone whether the term is renewed, and treats a renewal asked for twice as a weakness rather than a commitment.
attributes.taboos: No memorial object; no keeping of the dead; no measuring grief in years; and above all no regard for a burning body as exceptional, which the culture regards as the sentiment that started the famine.
attributes.cause: Economy and biology together: a fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated under it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, so the fastest race in the setting was also the shortest-lived and the most dominant at once.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Commonborn cooks, carries water and keeps the watch, and holds this culture without being a furnace body; what is shared is a local economy organised around heat, not an anatomy.
attributes.death_rites: Immediate, total and non-negotiable: the body is returned in full and nothing of it is kept, burned or traded, on the grounds that what a short life consumed should not be inherited.

name: Debt Line
summary: Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings, and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold. It exists because a line concentrated inside one household climbs faster than the same line spread across a village, and culling is the only lever a indebted house has.

attributes.language: House dialects keyed to the patronym rather than the region, so two people raised in one house can sound more foreign across a valley than to a foreigner.
attributes.values: The line outranks the person's preference; a debt stated aloud is a claim that survives the debtor; worth is measured in who is still willing to answer.
attributes.etiquette: No one is asked what they intend to do with a life. They are asked which debt they are working off, and the answer is a status, not a plan.
attributes.clothing: House colour on the left cuff only, deliberately small: the sleeve must be visible across a courtyard and unreadable at a distance, so a debt is legible to the household and not to a rival.
attributes.cuisine: Ranked plates - portions served in descending household order, the lowest place taking last. Refusing a portion is a statement about one's own standing and is watched.
attributes.art: Genealogical panels in the entrance hall, each branch cut out in the same hand and not replaced, so the absences are the artwork and the craft is in the never filling them in.
attributes.architecture: Houses built around a debt hall with one door per branch that no longer exists, bricked at knee height and never removed, so a visitor walks the whole list before meeting anyone.
attributes.festivals: The Naming Bond - the day a child's debt is spoken aloud in front of the whole house; an unbonded child is not excluded, only unaddressable, and is usually raised anyway.
attributes.marriage: Pairing is a debt transfer between two houses, recorded twice, once by each; the pair that appears in only one ledger is treated as unbound regardless of what its parents believe.
attributes.taboos: No household writes down why a branch ended; no one may be named as an heir before the reading is closed; and no debt is forgiven aloud, because a forgiven debt is a debt with no holder and the house cannot survive that.
attributes.cause: History: the Branch Cull is the single cause, and this culture is the custom layer that made a political financial decision into an inherited one.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: Commonborn's hundred-year life and realm-eight ceiling mean a line never dies out through old age while breeding, so culling rather than attrition was always available - and the culture picked it for financial reasons, not because the body compelled it.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The Tideculled line this culture is named for crosses races freely and carries no race of its own; the culture is a bookkeeping practice, and it is held by bodies it did not choose.
attributes.death_rites: The living debtor reads the name of the dead against the panel, and the house's outstanding sum is restated in the same breath, so grief and debt are never allowed to be separated in the telling.

name: Door Liturgy
summary: A practice, not a religion: a house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame under it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not. It exists because an unwritten law is not a weak law but an absent one, with no dial and nothing to push - so a community needing a guarantee of welcome cannot get one from the world and has to mark it itself.

attributes.language: A household register of invocations - phrases that are said at a threshold and mean a specific standing to be held by anyone who is let across, whatever their rank, office or cultivation.
attributes.values: A threshold has an obligation attached to it and the obligation survives the house that marked it; welcome is a property of the mark rather than of the person who keeps it; a door unmarked is a door no one is responsible for.
attributes.etiquette: A traveller is announced at the mark, not at the door, and is expected to state the household's mark unprompted; a traveller who cannot is let in anyway, because the culture's own doctrine holds that the mark exists for the guest's sake.
attributes.clothing: Guest-marked at the door - a visible alteration worn for the duration of a visit and removed at the threshold on departure, so that no one leaves a house still wearing its hospitality.
attributes.cuisine: The threshold meal, taken in the doorway and not inside, small and shared, which is this culture's one hospitality and the only thing it will offer a stranger without an arrangement.
attributes.art: The marks themselves, cut fresh each time the composition beneath a house changes and deliberately never cleaned or restored; an old mark in a new frame is the culture's central image and it is left up.
attributes.architecture: Every threshold is visible from the street, cut to a depth that can be re-cut, and every house keeps an outer room whose only function is to hold the mark and be readable from outside.
attributes.festivals: The Renunciation, held when a household learns its frame has changed: the old invocation is formally withdrawn in public and the new one cut the same day, and the withdrawal is read aloud by the household that marked it.
attributes.marriage: Two households, two marks and a threshold between them, and the union is held to have made one new mark and two obligations, neither of which the marriage dissolves.
attributes.taboos: No threshold entered without announcement; no mark removed rather than renewed; no household that has let a mark lapse; and no one is ever asked to state their cultivation at a door.
attributes.cause: Cosmology: the Refused Seating consumed a vacant slot on an absence and afterwards cannot be told from an empty one, so no procedure can certify any unclaimed capacity - and a community needing certainty of welcome had to build the guarantee at the door where it can be renewed.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: There is no body for which this practice is more or less urgent: a furnace body, a dense body and a body that cannot break a fast at all all stand equally at the threshold, and the culture's own etiquette forbids asking which is which before the door has decided.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The whole practice is a reading of a missing law, and laws do not belong to bodies - which is exactly why four races hold it, and why a traveller who cannot recite a household's mark is still let in.
attributes.death_rites: The household's mark is re-cut on the evening of the death - not removed, replaced - which this culture holds is the one duty that cannot be delegated and the one a mourner is trusted with.

name: Fluxwright
summary: An artistic guild that makes boundary art for the tiers, and re-masters its own symbols every generation so that nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw. It exists because a law scar opens where a group used to be written and no longer is, and the only durable defence against a hole shaped like a discipline is an art that is always one law short of being legible.

attributes.language: None spoken as a craft; the guild's working medium is marks on unwritable surfaces, and its teaching is conducted in gestures that a listener cannot record.
attributes.values: Nothing durable is made for one place; a work is finished when it would mean nothing to anyone who learned it elsewhere.
attributes.etiquette: An apprentice is not praised. Praise in this culture means the work has become readable, and it is followed immediately by a demand that it be broken.
attributes.clothing: Undyed, identical, and worn for as long as it lasts - the guild argues identity is the one thing a signature should never be attached to.
attributes.art: Marks laid so that the pieces only resolve into a figure when seen from a distance or in poor light, which is a technique of the Unwritten Law made into a rule rather than an accident.
attributes.cuisine: Cold and travelling: nothing that needs a settled hearth and no fixed recipe, with one dish the guild agrees on and changes every year so that no two generations are eating the same argument.
attributes.architecture: Studios with no corner and no door, so no interior of the guild's own making can be entered from outside by anyone reading a plan.
attributes.festivals: The Breaking, held when a set of work is deliberately destroyed in public, and the guild considers attendance optional and attendance cheerful to be a lapse.
attributes.marriage: A two-household compact, agreed because the guild has no internal lines of descent to appeal to and a household is the only unit in which anyone can inherit a tool or a debt.
attributes.taboos: No commissioned work with a named destination; no signature; no work held past its second generation without being broken; and no guild member explaining a piece to an outsider, on the grounds that explanation is the form of the art.
attributes.cause: Cosmology: the law scar left behind when a world gives up an imprint to pay upkeep, and the Daos in that world moving between tiers and taking their reading with them.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: The lineage carrying this gift - the oldest recorded one, kept in a single household so long that its name stopped describing a family and started describing a body - grants sustained pressure instead of impact, and the guild is made of the poor, the Cold and the long-lived, not of it.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The Tidecaller and Commonborn majority of this guild has no ancestry in it; the culture is an argument about how art should survive in a world that removes laws, and anyone may hold the argument.
attributes.death_rites: The body's face is turned to the wall and the room's marks are left unsmudged; the guild holds that a death in a studio leaves a composition behind whether or not anyone was working.

name: Passage Livery
summary: A credential culture: cloth and cut identify what a traveller is and what they may open, because a world boundary is not a wall but the edge of a law budget and the only thing anyone controls is permission to pass. It exists because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, nobody may levy a seat, and clothing is the one credential that costs nothing to check.

attributes.language: A road pidgin whose courtesy forms encode rank, and in which the form of address used by a speaker to a stranger is not politeness but a declaration of what the stranger may do next.
attributes.values: A credential is a promise and a promise is only as good as the door it opens; being legible matters more than being liked; a traveller owes the marshal nothing and the house everything.
attributes.etiquette: You are read before you are greeted, and a traveller who has misstated their own rank in the first hour has forfeited good standing for the rest of the road. Nobody corrects a stranger's rank for them.
attributes.clothing: The medium. Cloth, cut, colour and the manner in which it is worn are the whole of this culture's literacy, and it is a literacy that works across every race because no body reads it otherwise.
attributes.cuisine: Road food, identical in every licensed house on a route, which is deliberate: a traveller whose rank is being read should not also be working out what is in the bowl.
attributes.art: The half-cloak, dyed and cut by grade and re-dyed when a traveller's standing changes; the re-dye is done in public and the culture is very clear that the ceremony is the message.
attributes.architecture: Gate and courtyard architecture only, since this culture does not build: an extension of the guild house onto the road, with the grade visibly marked on the gate.
attributes.festivals: The Presentation, the one occasion on which every grade of the road appears together, ordered by cut, and the road's whole hierarchy is walked once in silence before anyone eats.
attributes.marriage: A contract of mutual standing, declared by the exchange of graded cloth and witnessed by the houses whose doors both parties may open - which in practice means a small, specific and consequential guest list.
attributes.taboos: No ungraded cloth worn outside a dwelling; no borrowing a grade; no correcting another traveller's rank on their behalf; and no grade held by a person who has not personally crossed the border it opens.
attributes.cause: History: the cost of existing rises about fortyfold per tier and only a body can be moved, so the count of who may pass became the only thing anybody could actually control - and cloth was the cheapest instrument available.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The strongest statement this culture makes is that the reading is not of the body, and its founding incident was a traveller refused entry for having the wrong anatomy rather than the wrong paper - a decision the guild reversed and thereafter graded by cut alone.
attributes.death_rites: The grade is cut from the clothing and returned to the house that issued it, and the body's own cloth is left unaltered; a traveller who is buried in borrowed rank is considered to have been misidentified rather than honoured.

name: Plain Dweller
summary: The commons of the Mortal Plains: a hundred-year body, a ceiling of eight realms and a frame seating only three laws, so nobody here expects to ascend and the work is judged by what survives the season. It exists because the region cannot afford a professional - the plough, the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands, so tenure is not an office, it is a queue.

attributes.language: A pidgin of nine valley speechforms with four working numerals and no agreed past; a person's history is carried by whoever outlived them, so the spoken record is the shortest that still functions.
attributes.values: Arriving before the season turns; a claim owed is a claim held; nobody's word outranks a shared measurement of grain.
attributes.etiquette: You are greeted by whatever you are carrying, not by name. Asking a person's history directly is rude; asking who taught them to plough is a greeting. Disputes are settled by both parties reciting the same measurement aloud.
attributes.clothing: Layered undyed plant and hide, patched at the shoulder and never at the knee. Colour is allowed once per person per decade, given by the village, and given for a funeral.
attributes.cuisine: One pot, one fire, one measure of salt. Every dish is a dilution of the same boiled grain with whatever the quarter's field offered, so a recipe is a record of a bad year as much as a good one.
attributes.art: Not image. Rope-lashing patterns on every structural joint, where a plain joint means a builder is careless and a four-strand joint names him; knots are read like signatures.
attributes.architecture: Sunk halls, earth-shouldered roofs, one shared lintel of softwood that is replaced rather than repaired, and a store whose floor stands above the highest flood line measured on a post outside.
attributes.festivals: The Threshold Count - on the last day the flood post stands clear, every household declares its own measure and the totals are read aloud; nothing else is marked in the year.
attributes.marriage: Two households exchanging a share of the seed for a share of the draft animal; the union is recorded in the fields, not in a register, and dissolves the same way.
attributes.taboos: No standing grain in the first month, so no one can corner it; no claim of descent that cannot be corroborated by a field still worked; and nobody reads aloud a count taken from another's store.
attributes.cause: Law composition first, environment second, biology last: three slots buy physical, life and qi and nothing else, so there is no season to plan against and no travel to plan for, and a hundred-year body under a realm-eight ceiling retires rather than is surpassed.
attributes.what_the_law_budget_forbids: No elemental craft, no travel between regions as a habit, no calendar - the clock drifts, so festivals hang off a measured flood instead of a date.
attributes.not_inherited_from_any_race: Commonborn is the majority body here and a minority one too: a settled household carries the Hearthborn concentration, which is an average of whatever the household took in rather than a purity.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Three bodies live under this one culture because the culture is a claim about land and water, not about anatomy - which is why a settler from the Spirit Peaks is Plain Dweller within a generation.
attributes.death_rites: The body is dressed in the one colour the village gave that decade and buried above the flood line facing uphill, because the plain is where people die and it is expected to flood. No property changes hands for a year.

name: Plains Widows
summary: A single-culture holding of wives left on the plains by the Peak Ascent, and the first culture in the setting built entirely out of an absence: no children of the absent are counted twice, and every ritual here is dated to the ascent rather than to a marriage. It exists because the movement was economic before it was spiritual, and the women who did not go were the ones the plains had to invent something for.

attributes.language: A plains speech with an entire tense reserved for departures, because the culture could not decide whether going was an event or a process and eventually settled on treating it as both.
attributes.values: An absent person is absent and is not spoken for; household continuity is maintained by standing in, never by substituting a name; the date of a departure is the important date in a life.
attributes.etiquette: No one is asked to speak for an absent partner and the refusal to do so is considered a courtesy. A child raised in a stand-in household answers to the household name without ever being recorded as the heir of either parent.
attributes.clothing: Whatever the household holds, worn with one deliberately mismatched outer piece kept unwashed and never explained, which is the culture's single visible badge and its most contested.
attributes.cuisine: Two servings prepared nightly and one eaten, on the reasoning that a household on the plains never knows when it will be two again; the uneaten serving is disposed of daily and never saved.
attributes.art: Lists, kept by the household and read only on the ascent's anniversary: who left, in what order, and what each was carrying. The lists are the only art this culture makes and they are frequently destroyed in floods.
attributes.architecture: Houses built with a separate small structure at the rear, used for nothing, kept roofed, and never explained to visitors except with the phrase that is needed until it is not.
attributes.festivals: The Reading of the Ascent - held once, on the anniversary, when every household on the plains reads its list aloud into the same space, and the reading takes longer than anyone expects.
attributes.marriage: A standing-in contract: a household takes responsibility for another's land, its children and its absences without ever taking the absent's name, and it is renewed annually rather than sworn for life.
attributes.taboos: No one speaks for an absent partner; no absent person's name is used to move property; no household refuses a standing-in request on grounds of religion; and no woman of this culture describes herself as waiting.
attributes.cause: History: cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks for spirit stone and jade because those resources cannot be found below, and did not come back - and the plains' populations thinned instead of recovering.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The Tidecaller and the Stoneborn hold this culture in numbers no plains village could produce on its own, and both arrived after the ascent; the culture is a response to a departure, and departures do not care what a body is.
attributes.death_rites: The list is appended to and read in full, including the departures, so a person's life is measured in three columns; no one is permitted to have the departures column removed.

name: Quench Order
summary: A discipline of Bankers rather than a school of thought, teaching the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, and closing permanently the moment the body is lit. It exists because the fastest bodies in the setting have no elemental law seated beneath them to spend into, so every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired.

attributes.language: Instructional and clipped; the tradition's entire literature is one-page drills copied by hand, and its teachers are disliked socially and consulted constantly.
attributes.values: Discretion over reach; a body spent early is a body still alive; no one teaches a technique they have not personally survived.
attributes.etiquette: The trained do not show what they can do. An unnecessary display in company is treated as a confession that the discipline was not taught properly, and is met with the particular silence used for people who cannot be corrected.
attributes.clothing: Layered heat-dissipating underclothes worn under borrowed outer layers; the discipline is judged on the fit of the inner layer, and its practitioners are recognisable by an unchanged outer garment through a great deal of exertion.
attributes.cuisine: Deliberately cold, on the argument that eating heat is borrowing from the furnace, and the tradition permits itself exactly one hot course per year at the watch.
attributes.art: Practice scars. The body is the record and a burn left deliberately is dated by the drill it came from, so a veteran is a calendar walked in flesh and photographs the history of the school.
attributes.architecture: Naked stone rooms with no fire at all, built where the ground is cold, because a room that must be cooled is cheaper than a body that must be repaired.
attributes.festivals: No festival. The tradition marks nothing - it holds that any ritual attached to self-damage is an invitation to do it for show, and that a discipline with a holiday becomes performance.
attributes.marriage: A negotiated schedule of agreed expenditure, worked out in advance and renegotiated without embarrassment; a pair who never renegotiate is treated as having stopped noticing what they are doing to each other.
attributes.taboos: No exercise in company without a spotter; no teaching an unlit body the closing step; no refusal of a spotter once offered; and above all no showing off, which the tradition treats as the actual cause of most deaths it prevents.
attributes.cause: Cosmology and biology meeting: elemental law is unwritten in the mortal tier, so fire affinity has no budget to draw on and every discharge is paid in flesh.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: This is the one culture a furnace body cannot simply choose not to join, because the overflow arrives whether or not anyone taught the technique - but the culture's ethics are authored by its teachers, and nothing in the body asks for discretion.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The Commonborn spotters and Water-drinkers who hold this culture outnumber the furnace bodies they serve, and the ethics belong to them; the race supplies the problem, not the manners.
attributes.death_rites: The body is spent out completely by the household in the furnace and nothing is returned; the culture has no other practice and regards retention as the impropriety.

name: Quiet Count
summary: The practice of keeping the house's real figures in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down. It exists because a house that files everything cannot be left alone, and the counting house it answers to owns the roads - so concealment is the price of continued independence.

attributes.language: A register the outer world cannot follow, not a cipher: sentences are ordered so that a listener repeats the market figures and the listener alone carries the household figures away.
attributes.values: A number written down is a number spent; the house's business is known to the house; teaching is the only gift that must be given freely, because a paid teacher is a witness.
attributes.etiquette: Question answering is a form of assault and is answered literally. Interrupting a member mid-count is the one genuinely unforgivable act, because it costs the count, and the count is the house.
attributes.clothing: The keeper of the count wears no distinguishing mark at all, which is the whole office; any marker would convert an invisible authority into a visible office that could be applied for.
attributes.cuisine: Two kitchens: one public and identical to every other house of its standing, one private whose contents are never enumerated and whose sole rule is that nothing served in it is written on the other kitchen's board.
attributes.art: Weaving whose patterns encode nothing, made deliberately on slow looms so that the hours are visibly empty - the art is an alibi for the hours the count actually takes.
attributes.architecture: Two buildings on one plot: a public house with a public door and a private one with no outside sign at all, connected by a stair narrow enough that a second person cannot pass.
attributes.festivals: The Open Room - once a year the private room is opened and everything in it is burnt in front of the membership, so the house proves annually that it holds nothing in writing.
attributes.marriage: Marriage asks the keeper for a number, not a date: what the joining costs the house, stated aloud once and never adjusted. Two figures always, from both houses.
attributes.taboos: The count may not be written, may not be shared outside the house, and may not be used to price a marriage; a house that puts a figure to that use is read as having already lost the office.
attributes.cause: Rivalry: the house that decided access is worth fighting over owns the roads, and the house that wanted to be left alone had to become undiscoverable to survive it.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: The lineage behind this practice was narrowed politically and crosses races freely, and it grants sustained perception rather than impact; the practice needs a head that will not be interrupted, not a body.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Two races are named here and neither supplies the culture; the culture is a professional secrecy, and the counting house is its employer rather than its author.
attributes.death_rites: On a keeper's death the count is walked, out loud, by three members who were each handed one third and never told what the other two hold, until the whole figure is reassembled once and then never spoken again.

name: Quiet Hour
summary: The custom of spending the last hour before a settlement falls silent at the trading floor, keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making. It exists because time runs between ten and a hundred times faster in the upper frames, so a labourer there would not live to see a contract mature - and the labour that does run is a hum nobody owns.

attributes.language: A working speech that is very nearly the one below it, altered in exactly one respect: no tense marks anything as finished, because nothing in this frame finishes on the scale a person experiences.
attributes.values: A thing begun is not a thing abandoned; silence is a held resource and not an absence; the floor is the only place all classes stand together and it is not to be privatised.
attributes.etiquette: Nobody approaches the floor before the hour has begun; nobody leaves it early; and the hum is never described, praised or improved upon, which is the single rule the community defends most fiercely.
attributes.clothing: A single undyed pattern supplied by the settlement, so that the floor reads as one surface and no body can be measured on it - this is a stated purpose, not a modesty.
attributes.cuisine: Everything served in a single sitting and nothing in courses, because a meal begun mid-hour cannot be counted against and this community will not be kept out of its own arithmetic.
attributes.art: The hum, and one fact about it: it is a transformed reading of the same law value the floor's instruments are running at, so the floor is the only place in the setting where a law in a strain is actually performed rather than described.
attributes.architecture: One level, one floor, no private rooms, and a ceiling left deliberately high so that the standing sound has somewhere to decay; the settlement argues for its own ugliness on acoustical grounds.
attributes.festivals: The Held Note, when the hour runs longer than any participant has previously lived through, and the settlement's entire practice is to continue holding it.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract entered into in the hour and thereafter renewed by attendance, on the reasoning that in a frame where nothing matures, the only durable arrangement is a habit someone keeps.
attributes.taboos: No private music; no speaking against the floor's sound; no ledger of attendance; and no explanation of the hum offered to a visitor - a refusal the settlement defends as its central etiquette.
attributes.cause: Cosmology: the Still Point is the one frame in the setting with real slack, fifteen seats against six laws, and a time-flow band that makes sustained personal attention expensive - so this culture is what happens to the observation of a strained law when an observer cannot leave.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: The court that governs this place speaks of it as a custom of the floor and not of a body, and the settlement's own founding roll admits no single race held it; what is shared is a frame and an hour, and a race does not own either.
attributes.death_rites: The hum stops for exactly the length of a held breath and resumes, and no one in the settlement will discuss why or speculate aloud; the practice is unanimous and the explanations are not.

name: River Notary
summary: A river culture whose authority is measured in documents a stranger would call private: a tally stick split with the person you are parting from is worth more than a sealed instrument, and courts have been known to prefer the broken stick. It exists because a split tally is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe, and because after the Iron Grief the ground no longer held any other record.

attributes.language: A continuous register with no written form, in which the exact wording of a contract is reproducible by two people who were both present, which is the community's definition of it having existed.
attributes.values: An agreement is witnessed or it is a rumour; a document that cannot be destroyed at both parties' wish is a trap; a person's word holds until they find a better one.
attributes.etiquette: Breaking a tally is done in the water, facing downstream, and the one who holds the half that sinks has spoken first. Everywhere else, the halves are cut cold and dry.
attributes.clothing: Waterproof outer layers with a deliberately wide opening at the front, because a river person must be able to shed everything in one motion and any garment that requires thinking about defeats itself.
attributes.cuisine: Raw, smoked and dried over the last available heat, with a shared drying rack above the landing that is treated as a public record of who is provisioned and who is not.
attributes.art: Tally-cut on anything that will take it, including roof beams, which is why a river house records its own debts on the structure of its own ceiling and reads its own history by lying down.
attributes.architecture: Piled stilt construction on the bank, deliberately demountable, so that a house can be moved whole when the river takes its ground - which it will, and which is treated as housekeeping rather than disaster.
attributes.festivals: The Float, on the first flood that reaches a carved post; the year is reckoned from it, because a river community's calendar is a measurement of water and no other authority.
attributes.marriage: A public exchange of halves, scored at a common door, so that a pair can be asked to produce the two halves and will answer in front of witnesses who are also owed food.
attributes.taboos: No sealed instrument on the water; no refusal to split a tally on request; and no written record kept that cannot be burned by the person who signed it.
attributes.cause: Economy: a three-slot mortal frame has no spatial law, so the ground cannot be relied upon to hold a boundary, a mark or a deed - only the current and the people on it can.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: The water-affinity body cannot take the Body path at all and was assembled for looking rather than for being hit, which makes its community the one with the most to gain from witnesses; the body chose perception, the culture chose the tally.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: A Stoneborn hull-crew and a Commonborn net-mender both hold this culture; what they share is a bank that keeps moving, not an anatomy.
attributes.death_rites: A split tally is cut for the dead and the half kept by the household, which is the only formal remembrance this culture performs and the reason a river house's rafters hold generations.

name: Shore Notice
summary: A tideline culture whose entire civic vocabulary is borrowed from the shore: nobody here is inside or outside, only high, low or turning. It exists because an unwritten temporal law means the clock drifts and no date is the same twice, so a community whose timekeeping depends on two tides a day learned early to speak in water instead of in dates.

attributes.language: A tidal register with four fixed reference points in place of tense, because a coastal community with a drifting clock needs words for where in a cycle a thing happened rather than for when.
attributes.values: The water's first word outranks any spoken claim; nothing is permanent and no one is expected to pretend otherwise; a thing returned by the tide is not recovered, it is lent.
attributes.etiquette: A question beginning with a date is treated as a misunderstanding rather than an insult and is answered by asking which water the asker meant. Nobody in this culture has ever agreed what a year is.
attributes.clothing: Layered, reversible, and worn wet to dry, so that clothing is a storage problem as much as a modesty one - the garment is chosen for how long it will take to become wearable again.
attributes.cuisine: Everything here is eaten within one tide cycle of being taken, which is a hard rule and the origin of the culture's entire cuisine: raw, cured, or cooked on standing stones, and never saved for a day nobody can name.
attributes.art: The shore itself, read: alignments of boulder, driftwood and post left in place through many tides and never once reset, so the art is a single work accumulating corrections made by the water.
attributes.architecture: Perched and demountable, with nothing at ground level that cannot be carried away in a surge; the culture considers a lost building a completed one and takes no builder to task for it.
attributes.festivals: The Turning, counted from whichever tide best matches the work rather than from a date, which means this festival is a different day every year and that is regarded as correct.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract timed to the tide rather than the season, renewed at the Turning, and the renewal is a standing item of business rather than an occasion.
attributes.taboos: No permanent building below the high-water mark; no date given as an account of anything; no refusal to release a net or a trap to the tide; and no claim that anything was lost.
attributes.cause: Cosmology: the law scar left where temporal_law used to be written in this frame, and the drift that makes a coastal calendar impossible - the culture is what a law scar looks like when a community has to live inside it.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: A water-affinity body is comfortable here and a fire-affinity body genuinely struggles, and both hold this culture because the tide sets the timetable for everybody identically - which is what makes it a culture rather than a habitat.
attributes.death_rites: A name is given to the water rather than to a plot, because nothing here can be held against the tide; the household keeps the memory and the shore keeps the date.

name: Stonewright
summary: A guild of builders held together by a cold-bathing practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies that were never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses. It exists because a fixed dense body can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and because the same density closes what a qi technique needs open - so the guild paid for a second, shorter ladder in its own currency.

attributes.language: A working dialect of the old tongue, deliberately conservative, because guild instructions are written once and copied for generations and nobody has the standing to modernise them.
attributes.values: A building outlives the guild; the body is a tool with a service life and is maintained like one; no member is asked to carry what a member's frame cannot carry.
attributes.etiquette: A builder does not accept a compliment and returns it as a measurement, because the culture has no way to praise someone that is not also a specification for the next one.
attributes.clothing: Layered, heavy, and cut for cold immersion - the guild's outer wear is designed to be removed instantly and is worn with the fastenings permanently undone for exactly that reason.
attributes.cuisine: Hard food, and food that must be chewed: bone broth, dense grain, salted fish, and a near-taboo on soft or prepared dishes that the guild attributes to the cold practice and which is probably learned taste.
attributes.art: The exposed frame itself. This guild's art is architecture that shows its joints, its ties and its repairs, and its masons are embarrassed by a wall that conceals how it stands up.
attributes.architecture: Mass, exposed tie-work, and buildings designed to be re-built in part rather than replaced whole; a structure in this guild's idiom is expected to have been repaired more than once and shows it.
attributes.festivals: The Cold Assembly, held once a year at the shortest cold, in which every member immerses publicly and no one is permitted to leave the water first - the practice's only social test.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract drafted around the work calendar rather than the season, since this guild's year is measured in immersion days and nothing else.
attributes.taboos: No member refuses an immersion in company; no guild instruction is rewritten by a single hand; no soft food is served at guild expense; and no member is permitted to describe the cold practice as hardening.
attributes.cause: Biology and its own contradiction: the density that makes a Stoneborn durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form, so a body built for load had to buy its cultivation in a currency no other body has.
attributes.biology_constrains_without_determining: Nothing in the body asks to be hardened or to keep its bones, and the guild's own etiquette refuses to describe the practice as hardening - a body that cannot be changed by qi was given a second method, not a nature.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Commonborn apprentices outnumber Stoneborn members in this guild's own roll and the admission rite is identical for both; what is shared is a trade and a peculiar cold habit, neither of which is inherited.
attributes.death_rites: The body's bones are kept and are never interred, on the argument that a hard body's frame is the only thing it leaves that is better than what it was born with; the rest is returned.

name: Threshold Builders
summary: A guild that builds and then guards doors, walls and thresholds, and takes as its measure that what it builds is tested from the other side. It exists because the Frame's own borders have to be held by somebody who has an interest in them being impassable and is also the party best able to build them.

attributes.language: A trade speech in which every word for a material also names the failure mode, which is why outsiders are understood and not trusted for the first season.
attributes.values: A boundary that has never been tested is decoration; a builder who has not stood on the far side of their own work has not finished it.
attributes.etiquette: A threshold is asked for once and granted once. Repeat requests are answered with the question of which side of the gate the asker intends to live on.
attributes.clothing: Plain, complete, and visibly repaired; a garment with a mended cuff is worn openly by this guild while the same repair in the court is a demotion.
attributes.art: The practice of carving a flaw deliberately into every lintel worked here, called the courtesy of the door, because a perfect door invites inspection and an imperfect one invites use.
attributes.cuisine: Field ration, unwrapped and eaten where the work stood, because a mason who eats indoors is a mason idle indoors. A completed threshold is marked with one shared meal laid at the footing and nobody is allowed to clear it up until the mortar has cured.
attributes.architecture: Everything is designed to be attacked: a hidden sill, a wall thick enough to be fallen back into, an arch deliberately weaker than its neighbours and load-tested by hand at the monthly rebuild.
attributes.festivals: The First Crossing, when a finished threshold is stood on from the far side before it is accepted, and the builder who is first across is laughed at for a year.
attributes.marriage: A contract of maintenance rather than a joining, drafted as a deed on the door itself: the marriage is lodged in the structure and the structure is obliged to be visited.
attributes.taboos: No gate left standing unwatched through its own trial; no threshold with no way to hold it closed by one person; and no work accepted that its builder has not crossed.
attributes.cause: History: the Eighteenth Bed Collapse left a bed of unmortared seats at realm eighteen, and the border is still crossed one person at a time because no institution has ever been able to hold it open.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Two Commonborn families among three hold this guild and the largest single clan behind it is Stoneborn; the culture is a commission and a habit, and it was placed there by a crossing failure rather than by a body.
attributes.death_rites: A body's weight is written into the gate it worked on - a notch, a maker's mark, a corner cut short - because this culture holds that the best argument for a wall is knowing who it cost.

name: The Unfiled
summary: The practices of people who are on no list: changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing. It exists because the counting house that answers a carriage trade with prices at its own rates cannot enumerate a trade whose good is unrecorded, and pressure from that side produced the most careful paperless culture in the setting.

attributes.language: A shifting register in which names are treated as consumables; a speaker is understood to be using a name that will be retired and nobody records which.
attributes.values: Nothing written is nothing owed; a name is a thing you use rather than a thing you own; obligation exists between people who are present and stops being enforceable the moment they are not.
attributes.etiquette: You are greeted by the name you were last called and never corrected; a question about a predecessor is not answered, however senior the asker, and the refusal carries no apology.
attributes.clothing: Nothing that persists - no ornament, no fixed dye, and items altered often enough that an item cannot be traced. This is a practical consequence of a paperless culture and not a preference.
attributes.cuisine: One dish cooked in the road and issued from a single vessel, with no table, no seats and no conversation permitted while eating; the culture is emphatic that this is about nobody learning who is present, not about austerity.
attributes.art: Absent. Deliberately, and with a stated position: this culture regards a fixed style as a filing system for faces, and its members change their mark every season so that a description of one of them is useless within a year.
attributes.architecture: Nothing built. This is a material absence with a cause and the culture's own argument is that it is not poverty - permanent structures are what a list is built out of.
attributes.festivals: The Turning of Names, held once a year in whatever place nobody local recognises, at which every present person retires the name they have been using and takes a new one, and the roll of retirements is never written.
attributes.marriage: A contract of the hour, declared to two witnesses and never repeated, and this culture is candid that the arrangement exists because a promise that can be proved is a promise that can be cited.
attributes.taboos: No permanent name; no written record of any kind, including of a death; no fixed dwelling; and no claim of ancestry, which cannot be shown and is therefore not claimed.
attributes.cause: Economy and politics: the counting house publishes credit, safe conduct and trading posts against exclusivity, and a community that would not accept exclusivity had to become impossible to enumerate.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: All four races are in it in proportion to nothing, because the only admission test is willingness to retire a name annually - which is a habit, and which a Stoneborn hull-crew and a Commonborn cook both had to learn the same way.
attributes.death_rites: The body is buried by people who did not know the name being buried, which is the standard and which the culture treats as the point of the rite rather than as a hardship.

name: Weight and Name
summary: An old seafaring trading culture that has never recovered a price list, because it concluded roughly four centuries ago that its own arithmetic was the greater hazard. It exists because a Void Serpent in any quantity is worth more than the ship carrying it, and a people that declined to price its most profitable cargo was therefore never worth raiding.

attributes.language: A trade speech with a vocabulary of weights and no vocabulary of prices, plus one term - the standing name - that covers every commercial arrangement the community has ever made.
attributes.values: A price is a claim about the future; a weight is a fact about the present; nobody in this culture is ever the first to say what a thing is worth.
attributes.etiquette: The first offer in any negotiation is a compliment and everyone knows it, so nobody makes one, and a buyer who names a figure first has forfeited standing in the market for a season.
attributes.clothing: Everything cut for balance rather than for appearance, in two weights so that a garment can be traded without either party knowing what the other weighs; the culture considers a well-fitted garment to be a commercial disclosure.
attributes.cuisine: A single dish, agreed once, changed by nobody, served to buyer and seller off the same board; this culture holds that a shared plate is a standing name in culinary form.
attributes.art: Ship decoration as a legal statement: every hull carries a design whose meaning is that nothing on board is registered anywhere, so it is read by every other port as a promise of its own honesty.
attributes.architecture: Everything portable, including the counting houses, which are built as owned vessels so that an accounting can itself be moved if a port becomes unsafe - the community's central institutional bet.
attributes.festivals: The Standing Name - the day a ship's marking is redone from scratch, with the community present, because a hull's statement must be made jointly and cannot be inherited quietly.
attributes.marriage: A two-household contract recorded in weights, never in money, and the two households' right to weigh is understood to pass to the pair - a transfer of the trade's only instrument.
attributes.death_rites: The hull's design is cut through in one line by a household that has no vessel, which is the community's only way of withdrawing a promise; everything else about a death is handled as ordinary.
attributes.taboos: No price list, ever; no inventory taken aboard by anyone else; no fixed term of contract; and no naming of what a cargo is worth, including in a will.
attributes.cause: History and cosmology together: this is the one surviving settlement of the people who carried Void Serpents out of the Spirit Peaks before the caravan trade collapsed - and the collapse was caused by the serpents' own law values writing a number that cannot be recorded, so what the settlement abandoned was the ledger.
attributes.why_it_is_not_a_race: Two of its four member races arrived after the settlement was founded and were admitted without argument, because the culture's only admission test is whether a person can keep a weight honest - a competence, not a body.
